name: Housing Almanac
description: An open, versioned index of public housing data.

entries.title: ABS Building Approvals, Australia
entries.description: The Australian Bureau of Statistics' monthly count and value of dwelling units and non-residential building approved, by state, territory and smaller areas — the leading indicator of new housing supply in Australia.

coverage.spatial: Australia (national, states and territories, smaller areas)

entries.attribution: Australian Bureau of Statistics, Building Approvals, Australia
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200. The page "Building Approvals, Australia" lists "Latest release Building Approvals, Australia, August 2026", with monthly previous releases and future release dates (the October 2026 release due 08/12/2026). The ABS "Total Value of Dwellings" release (June Quarter 2026 latest), which carries mean dwelling prices, is a candidate for a separate entry.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: https://www.abs.gov.au/website-privacy-copyright-and-disclaimer states "All material presented on this website is provided under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International licence, with the exception of" the Coat of Arms, ABS logo, trade marks, "unit record data (microdata)" and third-party content. This is a site-wide notice, not one specific to this release. The XLSX time-series format is assumed, and the ABS Data API and the small-area detail weren't checked.

entries.title: Census Building Permits Survey
entries.description: The Census Bureau's survey of new privately-owned residential construction authorized by building permits, published monthly and annually for the nation, regions, states, metropolitan areas, counties and individual permit-issuing places.

coverage.spatial: United States (national, regions, states, metropolitan areas, counties, permit-issuing places)
coverage.temporal: varies by geography (2025 annual data latest)

entries.attribution: U.S. Census Bureau, Building Permits Survey
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200 (curl with a browser user agent and headless Chromium). The page "Building Permits Survey (BPS)" says its purpose is "to provide national, state, and local statistics on new privately-owned" residential construction, offers files "in text format", and says "Annual data for 2025 was released on May 14, 2026". It notes that preliminary national and regional permits appear "in Table 1 of the New Residential Construction report". New Residential Construction (permits, starts, completions; census.gov/construction/nrc/) was not cataloged separately: the economy-almanac census-economic-indicators entry already names it.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: I found no explicit licence statement on census.gov; the citation guidance (https://www.census.gov/about/policies/citation.html) asks users to cite the Census Bureau. public-domain is asserted from the Bureau's status as a federal agency (17 U.S.C. 105). The monthly cadence and the XLSX format are assumed and weren't checked.

entries.title: Census Housing Vacancies and Homeownership (CPS/HVS)
entries.description: The Census Bureau's quarterly and annual estimates of rental and homeowner vacancy rates, the homeownership rate, and characteristics of units available for occupancy, from the Current Population Survey/Housing Vacancy Survey.

coverage.spatial: United States (national, regions, states, largest metropolitan areas)

entries.attribution: U.S. Census Bureau, Current Population Survey/Housing Vacancy Survey
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200 (curl with a browser user agent and headless Chromium). The page says the program "provides current information on the rental and homeowner vacancy rates, and characteristics of units available for occupancy" and that "the rental vacancy rate is a component of the index of leading economic indicators". It links a "Latest Quarterly Residential Vacancies and Homeownership Report", data tables, annual tables and an API section, and warns users to "exercise caution when interpreting HVS data collected during the COVID-19 pandemic". The latest quarter's date wasn't read from the page. The economy-almanac census-economic-indicators entry is a Census-wide umbrella and doesn't catalog this program's own page.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: I found no explicit licence statement on census.gov. The citation guidance (https://www.census.gov/about/policies/citation.html) asks users to "cite the Census Bureau as the source of the original data", and the privacy policy carries no copyright notice. public-domain is asserted from the Bureau's status as a federal agency (17 U.S.C. 105). Formats and geographic detail are assumed and weren't checked.

entries.title: CFPB Home Mortgage Disclosure Act (HMDA) Data
entries.description: Loan-level data on US mortgage applications, originations and denials reported under the Home Mortgage Disclosure Act, published by the CFPB (with the FFIEC) as modified loan/application registers, national snapshot and dynamic datasets, and aggregate reports.

coverage.spatial: United States (loan level; census tract, county, metro, institution)
coverage.temporal: 2017-present on the CFPB data publication site; earlier years on ffiec.gov

entries.attribution: Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, HMDA data
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200. The CFPB page "Home Mortgage Disclosure Act (HMDA) Data" says "Each year, millions of people apply for mortgages. Using HMDA data, we can learn what happened to the vast majority of those applications". It was last modified Oct. 16, 2026, and links the news item "2025 HMDA Data on Mortgage Lending Now Available" (Mar 31, 2026). The data-publication site https://ffiec.cfpb.gov/data-publication/ (HTTP 200, redirects to /data-publication/2025) calls HMDA "the most comprehensive publicly available information on mortgage market activity". It offers a weekly-updated "Dynamic National Loan-Level Dataset" and a snapshot dataset ("Data Freeze Date: June 2, 2026"), and says pre-2017 data are at ffiec.gov. The CFPB landing page is cataloged because the data-publication URL redirects to a different year each release.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: https://www.consumerfinance.gov/privacy/website-privacy-policy/ states "Information created by the CFPB is in the public domain and you may reproduce, publish, or otherwise use it without the Bureau's permission. Please consider appropriate citation to the Bureau as the source." The released files are compiled from filings by lenders and modified by the CFPB for privacy. The Data Browser API and file formats weren't checked.

entries.title: Eurostat Housing Statistics Database
entries.description: Eurostat's housing theme: harmonised EU statistics on house prices, housing conditions and costs (including overcrowding and housing cost overburden from EU-SILC), tenure, and census dwelling data, for EU member states and some neighbouring countries.

coverage.spatial: EU member states (plus some EFTA and candidate countries)

entries.license: CC-BY-4.0 (Eurostat copyright notice and free re-use of data)
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200 (curl and headless Chromium). The page is titled "Database - Housing - Eurostat", with the heading "HOUSING Database" and tabs for Overview, Database, Visualisations, Publications, Methodology, Census hub and a "Census dwelling grid". The dataset tree loads with JavaScript and its list of tables wasn't read, so the specific datasets named in the description (house price index, EU-SILC housing indicators) come from Eurostat's usual structure and weren't checked here. The quarterly cadence applies to the house price index; EU-SILC housing indicators are annual.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/help/copyright-notice says "The copyright for the editorial content of this website, which is owned by the EU, is licensed under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International licence", and that "All data published on Eurostat's website can be regarded as belonging to Eurostat for the purpose of their reuse", with exceptions for data on countries outside the EU, EFTA and candidate countries. The formats, API and bulk download are assumed from other Eurostat entries and weren't checked.

entries.title: FHFA House Price Index
entries.description: The Federal Housing Finance Agency's repeat-sales house price indexes for single-family homes, from national level down to census divisions, states, metro areas, counties, ZIP codes and census tracts, with data back to the mid-1970s.

coverage.spatial: United States (national, census division, state, metro, county, ZIP code, census tract)

entries.attribution: Source: FHFA House Price Index (FHFA HPI®)
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200. The page "FHFA House Price Index®" describes "a comprehensive collection of publicly available house price indexes that measure changes in single-family home values based on data that extend back to the mid-1970s from all 50 states and over 400 American cities", using "a weighted, repeat-sales statistical technique". FHFA is an independent federal agency, so its own output is a US Government work. The monthly cadence applies to the headline purchase-only index; other series are quarterly or annual. This wasn't checked per series.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: FHFA's Website Privacy Policy (https://www.fhfa.gov/about/fhfa-policies/website-privacy-policy), section "Copyright and Trademark Notice", states "Generally, information and materials produced by Federal agencies, including FHFA, are in the public domain and may be copied and distributed without permission". It excludes "marks for which there is a federal trademark as denoted by the ® symbol". "FHFA HPI®" is such a mark, so the name is trademarked though the data are not. The API terms (https://www.fhfa.gov/about/fhfa-policies/api-terms-of-service) bar implying endorsement and modifying content while still attributing it to FHFA. The formats weren't checked.

entries.title: HUD Annual Homelessness Assessment Report (AHAR) and Point-in-Time Counts
entries.description: HUD's annual report to Congress on homelessness in the United States, with the January Point-in-Time (PIT) counts and Housing Inventory Count (HIC) data files by Continuum of Care since 2007, and system performance data.
entries.publisher: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development, Office of Policy Development and Research

coverage.spatial: United States (national, state, Continuum of Care)
coverage.temporal: 2007-present for PIT and HIC data files

entries.attribution: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development, Annual Homelessness Assessment Report
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200. The page describes the AHAR as "a HUD report to the U.S. Congress that provides nationwide estimates of homelessness". It is "based on Homeless Management Information Systems (HMIS) data ..., point-in-time counts of people experiencing homelessness on one day in January, and data about the inventory of shelter and housing". It links "Point-in-Time (PIT) and Housing Inventory Count (HIC) data files (XLSX) since 2007" and "System Performance data files (XLSX) since FY 2015". The latest report seen is "2025 AHAR: Part 1 - PIT Estimates of Homelessness in the U.S." The counts are collected and submitted by local Continuums of Care. Whether HUD contractors helped draft the report wasn't checked.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: I found no HUD or HUD USER page that states a data licence. The HUD USER disclaimer (https://www.huduser.gov/portal/about/disclaimer.html) and privacy policy carry no copyright statement, and the 'Web Management and Web Policies' footer link now lands on a general HUD page. public-domain is asserted from HUD's status as a federal agency (17 U.S.C. 105), not from a HUD statement.

entries.title: HUD Fair Market Rents
entries.description: HUD's annual Fair Market Rents — estimates of 40th-percentile gross rents for standard-quality units by bedroom count for every metropolitan area and non-metropolitan county, plus Small Area FMRs by ZIP code — used to set Housing Choice Voucher payment standards and other program rents.
entries.publisher: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development, Office of Policy Development and Research

access.auth_note: The FMR and Income Limits API needs a free account and access token; the web pages and files do not.

coverage.spatial: United States (metropolitan areas, non-metropolitan counties, ZIP codes for Small Area FMRs)
coverage.temporal: varies; fiscal years 2023-2027 shown on the page, older years in the history section

entries.attribution: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development, Fair Market Rents
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200. The page "HUD Fair Market Rents (40th Percentile Rents)" says FMRs "are estimates of 40th percentile gross rents for standard quality units within a metropolitan area or nonmetropolitan county" and take effect "at the start of the federal fiscal year (generally October 1)". The latest set is FY 2027 ("Click Here For FY2027 FMRs"). It announces that FMRs and Income Limits "are now available via an application programming interface (API)", which needs an account and access token (https://www.huduser.gov/portal/dataset/fmr-api.html).
Licence checked 2026-10-31: I found no HUD or HUD USER page that states a data licence. The HUD USER disclaimer (https://www.huduser.gov/portal/about/disclaimer.html) and privacy policy carry no copyright statement, and the 'Web Management and Web Policies' footer link now lands on a general HUD page. public-domain is asserted from HUD's status as a federal agency (17 U.S.C. 105), not from a HUD statement. Formats are assumed and weren't checked.

entries.title: Housing and Land Survey of Japan
entries.description: The Statistics Bureau of Japan's five-yearly sample survey of dwellings and households: housing stock, vacant dwellings, tenure, dwelling structure and condition, and land holdings, for Japan and its prefectures and municipalities.
entries.publisher: Statistics Bureau of Japan (Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications)

coverage.temporal: survey years 1998-2023 listed on the English page

entries.license: PDL-1.0 (Public Data License Version 1.0, Statistics Bureau terms of use; CC-BY-4.0 compatible)
entries.attribution: Statistics Bureau of Japan, Housing and Land Survey
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200. The English page "Housing and Land Survey" lists the 2023 Survey ("Outline of the 2023 Housing and Land Survey of Japan", sampling and reliability notes, explanation of terms, and "Survey Results of the Housing and Land Survey (Statistical Tables)"), then earlier rounds for 2018, 2013, 2008, 2003 and 1998. The survey runs every five years; the schema has no quinquennial value, so cadence is irregular. The statistical tables link to e-Stat, which wasn't opened.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: https://www.stat.go.jp/english/info/riyou.html says content "is possible to use ... under the use condition based upon the "Public Data License (Version 1.0)" (PDL1.0)", that it "may be freely used, copied, publicly transmitted, translated or otherwise modified" and that "Commercial use of Content is also permitted", and that "numerical data and data in Simple tables, graphs, and so forth are not subject to copyright". The CC BY 4.0 compatibility is the Japanese government's general statement about PDL 1.0 and wasn't re-read here. The formats are assumed and weren't checked.
